body.text: Kemmerer Unit 1 is a Natrium reactor plant in Lincoln County, Wyoming, about 3 miles southwest of Kemmerer.
body.anchor: approximately 3 miles (4.8 km) southwest of Kemmerer, Wyoming

body.text: It is licensed under 10 CFR Part 50, and this PSAR supports the construction permit application.
body.anchor: is requesting approval for a construction permit of an 840 megawatt thermal

body.text: The plant is built as part of the DOE Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program.
The reactor uses sodium-bonded metallic fuel with HT9 cladding, which is a high chromium martensitic steel.
body.anchor: The reactor uses sodium-bonded metallic fuel with high chromium martensitic steel (HT9) cladding

checks.q: What is the licensed thermal rating described for Kemmerer Unit 1?
checks.x: The PSAR describes an 840 MWt reactor. The 500 figure is net electrical output in megawatts electric, available through the salt storage system.
checks.anchor: The Natrium reactor plant is an 840 MWt pool-type sodium fast reactor

checks.q: What lets the plant vary its supply to the grid while reactor power stays constant?
o: The molten salt energy storage system
checks.x: The molten salt storage system lets grid output vary up to 500 MWe net while reactor power stays constant.
checks.anchor: molten salt energy storage system which enables the plant to vary its supply of energy to the grid

body.text: The reactor operates near atmospheric pressure, and pumps circulate sodium through the core.
body.anchor: The reactor operates near atmospheric pressure, circulating sodium through its core with pumps

cells: Upward flow through the core assemblies
rows.anchor: flows upwards to remove the heat generated from the fuel pins

cells: Intermediate heat exchangers in the reactor pool
rows.anchor: via intermediate heat exchangers located in the reactor pool
Salt System (NSS) via sodium-salt heat exchangers
Energy Island (EI) hot salt storage tank for thermal
The heat stored in the hot salt tank is used to generate steam

body.text: During startup and shutdown the intermediate loop rejects heat to the atmosphere through the Intermediate Air Cooling System sodium-air heat exchanger instead of the salt path.
body.anchor: to the atmosphere via the Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC) sodium-air heat exchanger during startup and shutdown

checks.q: Where does heat cross from primary sodium to intermediate sodium?
o: Intermediate heat exchangers in the reactor pool
checks.x: Heat moves from the primary loop to the intermediate loop through the intermediate heat exchangers in the reactor pool.
checks.anchor: via intermediate heat exchangers located in the reactor pool

checks.q: Where does the intermediate loop send heat during startup and shutdown?
o: To the atmosphere through the IAC sodium-air heat exchanger
To the hot salt tank only
checks.x: The intermediate loop transfers heat to the NSS for normal steady operation, and to the atmosphere through the IAC during startup and shutdown.
checks.anchor: sodium-air heat exchanger during startup and shutdown

body.text: The Nuclear Island contains the reactor and its supporting systems.
body.anchor: The NI, which contains the reactor and its supporting systems

body.text: The Energy Island contains the thermal energy storage tanks, steam generator, feedwater system, condenser, turbine, and supporting systems.
body.anchor: thermal energy storage tanks, steam generator, feedwater system, condenser, turbine, and supporting EI systems

body.text: The salt system physically connects the islands and stores excess thermal energy, so steam generation can run independently from reactor power operations.
body.anchor: providing a buffer that allows steam generation and thermal energy storage operations

checks.q: How are Energy Island structures, systems, and components classified?
checks.x: The PSAR classifies EI SSCs as non-safety-related with no special treatment (NST).
checks.anchor: The EI structures, systems, and components (SSCs) are classified as non-safety-related with no special treatment (NST)

body.text: The PSAR names near-atmospheric operating pressures, always-on passive air cooling, and inherent reactivity feedback as reliable inherent and passive safety features.
body.anchor: near-atmospheric operating pressures, always-on passive air cooling

body.text: Safety functions are made integral to the reactor vessel, and support equipment moves to separate structures, which simplifies the reactor building.
body.anchor: Safety functions are made integral to the reactor vessel

checks.q: Which is one of the safety features the PSAR lists for the design?
checks.x: The PSAR lists near-atmospheric pressure, always-on passive air cooling, and inherent reactivity feedback.

summary.text: Kemmerer Unit 1 is an 840 MWt pool-type sodium fast reactor with molten salt energy storage and up to 500 MWe net to the grid.
summary.anchor: The Natrium reactor plant is an 840 MWt pool-type sodium fast reactor

summary.text: Heat flows from core to primary sodium, to intermediate sodium, to salt, and then to steam.
summary.anchor: The heat stored in the hot salt tank is used to generate steam

summary.text: The Energy Island is non-safety-related with no special treatment.
summary.anchor: The EI structures, systems, and components (SSCs) are classified as non-safety-related with no special treatment (NST)

passages.quote: The Natrium reactor plant is an 840 MWt pool-type sodium fast reactor (SFR) that contains a compact and simple safety envelope and a molten salt energy storage system which enables the plant to vary its supply of energy to the grid, up to 500 megawatts electric (MWe) net, while maintaining constant reactor power.
The EI structures, systems, and components (SSCs) are classified as non-safety-related with no special treatment (NST).
